reason:
Three parts, verified separately. TWO SURVIVE WHOLE, ONE SURVIVES IN HALF.

(1) RETRY - SURVIVES. grep for data-act="retry" returns exactly two source hits: render-b.js:1545 (the draw) and interaction-check.mjs:2198, which only counts it (slow.way === 1). states["loading-slow"] calls states.loading() and registers no listener; wireOwner is called at 1139 and 1005 only, never on this state, and no delegated [data-act] handler in render-b.js or render-core.js reaches it. Driven at 390x844 on ?v=approach&state=loading-slow: click and Enter both leave #tl.outerHTML byte-identical, .b-field aria-busy stays "false", nothing changes 0.9s or 3.2s later, and document.activeElement parks on <button class="b-act" data-act="retry">. There is no .b-live in the state at all - the only role=status is the whole .b-field, so the retry button sits INSIDE the live region rather than being announced by one. Tab cycles between exactly one focusable and body. It is the sole offered move in the one state whose subject is failure, and render-b.js:470-471 writes the rule it breaks directly above inert(): 'Anything not built is inert text, never a focusable promise.' Not a gate restatement - the gate asserts existence only.

(2) DATA-SPACING - SURVIVES, and is the serious one. Zero selectors anywhere read it: enumerating every CSSRule in the built master returns [] for /spacing/ in selectorText (the only b.css hits are letter-spacing declarations); render-b.js contains the string 'spacing' zero times; render-core.js contains it only as preset values and the console control at 231-251. Driven: ?spacing=measured vs ?spacing=even at 1440x960 owner-flight gives identical body attribute reads (measured/even) and IDENTICAL geometry - item tops [570.28, 696.28, 948.28, 1074.28, 1200.28, 1452.28, 1704.28] both times, .b-measure height 1536 both, scrollHeight 2130 both, and #tl.outerHTML byte-identical at 8691 chars. Same at 390x844 state=phone: [577.36, 661.36, 829.36, 913.36, 997.36, 1165.36, 1333.36] both. The console is worse than the finding says: in the compiled console.html 'Even rhythm' is not decoration, it is <button type="button" class="choice" data-choice="spacing" data-value="even" aria-pressed="false">, it FLIPS #deck's data-spacing from measured to even when pressed, aria-pressed and all - and the deck's item tops stay [589, 682, 867, 960, 1053, 1238, 1424] before and after. One of the four named decisions, carried by all three presets, given a paragraph of help copy ('The honest cost of measured is holes'), published as a live pressed-state control, and wired to nothing. This is distinct from space-ladder-does-not-cover-the-property-that-spaces, which is about gap tokens.

(3) .B-SWITCH - SURVIVES ON CHROME, REFUTED ON NAMES. The chrome half is exact and worse in the frames than in prose: .b-switch computes border 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16), border-radius 6px, min-height 32px - character-for-character the same three values .b-act computes - with font-weight 600, cursor auto, no role, and no hover response, while .b-act has cursor pointer and a hover border/background. Cropped at 390x844 owner-flight the pill 'Mara & Finn ONE OF THREE' sits at y=45 with the three real buttons at y=88, 43px directly beneath it, same border, same radius, 33px vs 39px tall: it reads as a fourth control in a stack of four. At 1440 it is the same pill with 405px of air to 'Add a moment' (not the 560px claimed - a wrong number, not a wrong observation). But the accessible-name half is FACTUALLY WRONG and I refute it: measured off Chrome's full AX tree at 390, 768 and 1440, the disclosure's name is "BEHIND YOU 3 moments +" WITH the separating space, not 'Behind you3 moments'; and .b-switch is display:flex with gap:8px, so its two children render at x=33..115 and x=123..223 - an 8px visual gap - and reach the AX tree as two separate StaticText nodes, 'Mara & Finn' and 'ONE OF THREE'. 'Mara & Finnone of three' is a textContent artefact of the seat's measurement method, not something any reader sees or hears. Two smaller inaccuracies: the span carries NO tabindex attribute (the finding says tabindex -1), and there is no b.css:577-598 defect of the kind implied - the box is at 577-590.

No constraint is touched by any surviving part: no hue, no weight, no family, no reopening of the locked direction. The verdict is confirmed on (1) and (2) outright and on (3)'s chrome only; the separator fixes in the proposed remedy should be dropped, because applying them would insert a double space into a name that is already correct.
sharpenedFix:
Three fixes, one of them cut down.

(1) Retry. Take the wired branch, not inert(). loading-slow is the guest's failure state and inert text there is a dead end with no move at all. On press: set .b-field aria-busy="true", restore the four .b-skel bars and 'Bringing in what is ahead.', keep focus on the button (do not steal or move it), and announce through a .b-live status node that must be ADDED - the state has none today, and the .b-field's own role="status" cannot serve, because a live region that contains the button pressing it is a re-announcement of the whole screen. After the stall interval put 'Still not arriving. The plan has not been deleted, and the link still works.' into .b-live. Then close the gate hole: add 'loading-slow' to the every-control-does-something list at interaction-check.mjs:1123-1147 AND drop document.activeElement from the sameness comparison at 1132/1140, so a press that only moves focus can never read as alive.

(2) data-spacing. Delete it. Implementing 'even' is not the 15-line branch the finding implies: place() derives the tick rail, the stack runs, the 'days away' unit sentences and the collision clamp from data-away, so an even branch is a second geometry engine plus a fourth room, plus shots, plus gate coverage - a build, and one that argues against the direction's own thesis that a pixel is a real unit of time. Removing it costs four lines and buys the one thing the console is for: every control in it does what it says. Cut data-spacing="measured" from build.mjs's <body> line, 'spacing' from the parameter list at build.mjs, the spacing key from all three presets at render-core.js:231-233, and the whole control object at render-core.js:246-251. Then re-title the console honestly: it publishes THREE named decisions, not four. If the founder wants the fourth back, it returns as a shipped room with its own shot, never as an unbacked knob.

(3) .b-switch. Fix the chrome only. Drop border, border-radius, min-height and padding from .b-switch (b.css:577-590) and keep display:inline-flex with the 8px gap, so the project name sets as weight-600 text beside .b-where's mono workspace and the bar reads left-to-right as a breadcrumb - place, then project, then the actions - rather than as four pills of which one is dead. That single change is the whole fix: it removes the false affordance at every width including the 390 stack where the pill sits 43px above three identical real buttons. DO NOT apply the two separator edits in the proposed remedy - bar()'s [projectName, ' ', span] and behindBlock()'s ' ' + past.length + ' moments'. Both names already compute with correct spacing in the AX tree ('BEHIND YOU 3 moments +'), and adding literal spaces to a flex row that already has gap:8px and to a name the accname algorithm already separates would ship a double space where the defect never was.
